messages:
erin: Proposal: add automated cordon -> taint -> drain workflow triggered by GPU health signals (ECC/Xid spikes). goal is reduce noisy flaky-card churn and surface replacement tickets, but be safe with PDBs and slurm jobs.

max: +1. can you sketch the signal thresholds? we need to avoid false positives during bursts.

erin: sketch: leaky-bucket counter per GPU node (prometheus). increment on Xid/ECC events scraped from node-exporter + nvidia-smi exporter. heuristic: if Xid_count > 3 within 10m => cordon+taint (NoSchedule). if Xid_count > 10 within 30m OR ECC_corrected > 100 in 1h => drain and mark for replace. immediate drain only if continuing failures after cordon window.

priya: question: how do we handle slurm? draining k8s nodes is ok, but slurm jobs should be requeued gracefully.

erin: plan: two-path flow. for k8s nodes: kubectl cordon <node>; add taint `gpu-failure=true:NoSchedule`; send optional annotation with reason. after cordon, monitor pod eviction progress respecting PDBs; if pods stuck for > 15m, escalate to ops for manual intervention. for slurm nodes (same physical hosts in hybrid cluster): call `scontrol update NodeName=<node> State=DRAIN Reason="gpu_health_auto"` + requeue running jobs where checkpoint available, otherwise notify owners via pager.

max: sample kubectl sequence we tested in sandbox:```
kubectl cordon node-123
kubectl taint nodes node-123 gpu-failure=true:NoSchedule
kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=15m
```
note: `--force` avoided except for emergency.

priya: what about DaemonSets that manage GPUs? also local-storage flags can kill important state.

erin: yes: we will maintain an allowlist of daemonsets and critical local storage pods (checkpoint writer). drain will skip those and we will run a graceful handoff hook for checkpoint writers (curl to sidecar to flush).

jason: infra-bot should create a ticket and push a slack thread to the owning team when we cordon, not just when we drain. otherwise owners miss early signals.

infra-bot: automated action: cordon detected on node-123 (region-us-west-2). created ticket INFRA-4271. alert: GPU_XID_RATE firing for node-123. link: https://pm.redwood/in/INFRA-4271

dave: How do we avoid flapping? some nodes emit single Xid every few days.

erin: add hysteresis: cordon cooldown 1h after auto-cordon, and a separate auto-uncordon if node is healthy for 24h and no ticket marked replace. also maintain running median of Xid rate and require >2x baseline to trigger.

max: telemetry: we'll need extra labels: node pool, model serving vs dev, region, dedicated=true. for dedicated pools we may prefer immediate replacement rather than draining to keep SLA.

priya: also need to check capacity before draining dedicated pools. if not enough spare GPUs in same region, postpone drain and escalate to capacity-oncall so they can schedule reserved burst or move traffic.

erin: good point. flow includes capacity check via our capacity service: if spare_gpus(pool, region) < threshold -> keep cordoned but do not drain; escalate to capacity team. the ticket will include capacity hints and nearest compatible pool.

jason: ops playbook snippet idea (to add to docs):
- cordon event -> infra-bot creates ticket -> owner notified
- 30m watch window for pod evictions and slurm job requeues
- if errors continue -> auto-drain + mark replace
- on replace: mark node as retired in inventory, kick replacement pipeline (hw swap or reprovision VM)

max: metrics/alerts to add to prometheus:
- gpu_xid_count_total (per gpu, per node)
- gpu_ecc_corrected_total
- gpu_health_auto_action_total{action=cordon|drain|uncordon|replace}
- node_auto_cordon_cooldown_seconds

priya: what's the tolerance for requeues? for long-running slurm training we prefer checkpoint+requeue instead of cancel. add logic: if job has checkpoint file in /checkpoint and last checkpoint < 1h -> requeue, else cancel with notify.

erin: implementation notes:
- signal ingestion: node-exporter + nvidia-dcgm exporter -> prometheus rule -> alertmanager -> infra-controller service (k8s controllerrun).
- infra-controller will run as deployment with leader election, use k8s api + slurm rpc (ssh to slurmctl) for hybrid actions.
- controller will write annotations to node resource with action history.

infra-bot: action: created runbook PR https://git.redwood/repo/infra-auto-gpu-cordon/pull/12

dave: safety checks: ensure controller requires two independent signals before drain (prometheus Xid + nvidia-smi output > some threshold) to avoid noisy exporter bugs.

erin: agreed. also add a canary rollout of automation: start in `dev` pool for 2 weeks, then `staging`, then `prod` with gradual % of pools opted-in.

max: ops question: who gets paged for cordon vs drain? cordon -> slack alert + non-urgent ticket, drain -> page oncall. put that in runbook.

priya: minor: include region capacity note in ticket and a short ETA for replacement if we schedule hardware.

jason: love it. next step: infra-controller PR + runbook PR. erin can you open them and assign reviewers?

erin: will open PRs today, assign @max @priya for review. starting with canary in `dev` pool only. thanks everyone :+1:

infra-bot: reminder scheduled: canary rollout plan meeting 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC. calendar invite sent.
